notices.short_title: HH112FTRF - Fort Washington Armory Roof Replacement - SI
notices.description: Special inspection services for the partial replacement of the Fort Washington Armory Roof. The objective is to provide safe shelter and an improved quality of life for its occupants. The existing roof has experienced water infiltration, and related damage throughout. This condition is beyond repair and the existing roof must be partially replaced. The current roof leakage is a safety hazard and disrupts the quality of life of the residents, staff, and general public.Please see Scope of Services Memo for more information.

notices.short_title: HVAC Renovation
notices.description: This Project consists of the removal and replacement of AC-3 which serves the second and third floors. New supply and return ductwork will be installed. The Third Floor MER will be extended to accommodate the removal and installation of the new AHU. New Controls and two new return fans will be provided. Existing Lighting and Ceiling mounted devices affected by the removal and installation of new duct work will be removed, stored and re-installed upon the completion of the new ceiling installation. Existing sprinkler heads and piping in 3rd Floor MER will be replaced with new, 2nd and 3rd Floor corridor sprinkler piping will be secured properly to slab. New lighting will be provided in 3rd MER. In the 3rd Flor MER, new humidifier, Hot water coil and associated hot water piping with valves and controls, condenser water piping will be provide for new AHU. Community Board #: Manhattan 7

notices.short_title: BWT-JOC-26-PWH: HVAC Work
notices.description: The work under this contract is for HVAC Work under a series of small to medium size construction projects at all Bureau of Wastewater Treatment (BWT) Wastewater Resource Recovery Facilities. In addition to large capital construction projects, BWT has an ongoing need to accomplish smaller, straight forward construction projects at its facilities. Without Job Order Contracts, for each such project, the BWT must prepare complete contract documents and execute the required steps through the competitive bid process. Procuring the construction through this traditional design-bid-build process takes considerable time. Many of the projects are essential to maintain the operation of BWT facilities. The considerable time it takes to get contracts in place can jeopardize the continuation of service and, in some cases, permit the problem to worsen and result in additional costs. This Job Order Contract allows BWT to accomplish the much-needed projects in a fraction of the time while paying competitive prices for the work.
